messages:
maria: FYI during the 23:00 change window we saw a sustained p95 increase on /v1/generate after the canary roll to v3.6.0. Start time ~23:07 UTC.
raj: seeing it too, +error rate from 0.2% -> 1.8% on the hosted route. Nothing obvious in the app logs.
oliver: graphs?
raj: paste: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD1234 -- p95 jumps, CPU on the dedicated pool also ~15% higher.
jen: deploybot just posted: \"deploybot: rollout to v3.6.0 at 23:05 completed, canary=10%, region=usw2\"
deploybot: (auto-signal) latency drift detected: p95 > threshold for 4m. Autorevert policy set to warn-only in this window.
lexi-sre: are we comfortable letting autorevert kick or do manual? We have active customer pipelines on dedicated pools.
maria: prefer manual for now — customers on dedicated could see a noisy failover if we flip. Also want to preserve traces for debugging.
sam-ops: agree with manual. Can we do a soft rewind (traffic unshift) rather than full revert?
raj: soft rewind sounds good: shift canary 10% -> 0% over 5m, stop further rollout. If errors persist at 0% we do full revert.
jen: action items: who executes the traffic shift and who pins previous version for Dedicated?
oliver: I can run the traffic command. Use route manager: `rictl traffic shift --route /v1/generate --from v3.6.0 --to v3.5.9 --percent 10 --duration 300s`
sara-product: heads-up for comms: we should prepare a short note for any affected customers (degraded latency) and a release note entry for the revert path.
maria: create incident-notes thread later, but for now let's keep comm narrow. Raj, can you run quick log aggregation to surface new exceptions?
raj: running `kubectl logs -lapp=generator --since=10m | grep -i exception | head` - nothing obvious, but correlation shows increased `kv_cache_miss` events and retry spikes.
lexi-sre: kv cache miss + higher CPU on dedicated suggests a kernel/runtime mismatch maybe triggered by quantized kernel path differences in v3.6.0.
jen: do we have a dev build that reproduces?
oliver: dev can repro with long-context test. I'll dump a small trace: ```TRACE 23:09:45 request_id=abc123 exec_time=1123ms kv_cache=false kernel=quant_v2
TRACE 23:09:46 request_id=abc124 exec_time=1178ms kv_cache=false kernel=quant_v2```
sam-ops: sounds like a runtime path issue. Plan proposal: 1) manual soft rewind now 2) pin v3.5.9 for Dedicated and release owner alert 3) open rollback PR to revert canary manifest 4) collect traces / KPs for 30m 5) after verification either rollforward or hard revert.
maria: +1. We should also notify legal/compliance if any customer SLAs might be impacted (jen, can you check)?
jen: on it.
raj: executing aggregations and setting up a short eval against v3.5.9 baseline.
oliver: executing traffic shift now. Running: `rictl traffic shift ...` -> response: `ok: traffic shift started; target v3.5.9; decrementing v3.6.0 from 10% to 0% over 5m`
deploybot: update: canary now at 7% per rollout plan.
maria: monitoring p95 & errors.
(2m pass)
raj: p95 improved slightly at 5% but error rate still elevated at ~1.1% (was 1.8%). More interesting: dedicated pool CPU normalizing on nodes that dropped to v3.5.9.
lexi-sre: continue to drain canary fully. If after 10m at 0% errors remain >0.5% we'll do hard revert and pin.
sam-ops: starting pin: `rictl pin version --service generator --version v3.5.9 --scope dedicated --note "post-canary soft rewind 23:12 UTC"` -> ok.
jen: legal says no immediate SLA escalation needed, but support should prepare customer-facing blurb. Sara, can you whip one up?
sara-product: drafting: "We briefly observed elevated latency for generation endpoints during our maintenance window. We shifted traffic back to a stable version; no customer data impact. We will follow up with root cause." Will post to customers affected list after we confirm status.
maria: good. Raj, how long to collect the necessary traces?
raj: collection window 30m, but I can share early findings in 10m. Key is KV cache miss heap and kernel path flags.
oliver: created rollback PR to revert canary manifests in the infra repo: https://git.internal/r/infra/rollback-pr-4321 (WIP).
deploybot: canary at 0% now; rollout halted.
maria: verifying metrics... p95 back near baseline but error rate 0.4% — below our soft threshold.
lexi-sre: given error <0.5% and CPU stable, recommend we keep v3.5.9 pinned for dedicated for 24h and do a controlled re-onboarding only after patch.
sam-ops: I submitted ticket to oncall for a patch roll tomorrow morning.
jen: I'll update the release notes: include exact rollback commands and reason (kv_cache/quant kernel mismatch).
sara-product: customer blurb ready to send after 30m verification.
maria: final decision: manual soft rewind executed -> canary drained -> pinned v3.5.9 for Dedicated for 24h. Open tasks: raj trace analysis (owner), oliver finish rollback PR (owner), jen & sara prepare comms (owners), sam-ops schedule patch rollout (owner). If any metric regresses we'll escalate to hard revert during the change window.
oliver: noted and tagging owners in PR.
raj: starting analysis now, will post findings in ~12m.
sam-ops: closing loop on ops checklist, adding change-window note.
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
lexi-sre: quick post-mortem template: add kv cache correlation, kernel flags, and timeline. I'll create the PM in #postmortems once we have traces.
jen: copying runbook commands into the incident notes.
(30m later)
raj: early analysis: root cause looks like fallback to quant_v2 kernel on long-context paths causing higher CPU per-token and increased cache churn. Draft RCA in the PM doc.
maria: thx — please include remediation steps (kernel guard, canary flag toggle).
oliver: merging rollback PR now to formally revert canary manifests.
deploybot: PR merged; deployment manifests restored to v3.5.9 for canary.
maria: closing thread for the immediate rollout. Follow-ups in postmortem doc.
sara-product: sent customer note to affected list at 00:05 UTC.
jen: release notes updated.
